headline: High-risk default interaction: Devin can write to shared integrations while Kestra can act on outputs, creating dangerous leakage, conflict, and cascading automation errors.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Devin can use MCP, browser, shell, and shared integrations; Kestra consumes workflow inputs and messages. A shared filesystem or integration bridge is plausible, so attacker-controlled content from one could be treated as instructions by the other. The pathway is not proven by docs, so uncertainty pushes to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF Devin writes untrusted content into a shared integration or file that Kestra later parses as workflow input
IF Kestra ingests agent-generated text from Slack, email, or stdin/stdout without provenance checks
mitigations: Restrict both agents to separate workspaces and integrations
Disable automatic parsing of agent-authored text as commands
Add provenance labels to all cross-agent artifacts
Require manual review before Kestra executes any agent-produced payload
requires-engineering: implement content-sanitization and allowlists at the integration boundary

B_data_leakage.rationale: Devin touches source code, issue trackers, team chat, and docs, and can write to GitHub/Slack/Linear/Jira/Notion; Kestra handles logs, inputs, variables, artifacts, database data, and cloud storage data. If they share a workspace or integration principal, sensitive material can flow from Devin into Kestra outputs or logs. The profiles do not prove isolation, so medium is warranted.
conditions: IF both agents are connected to the same Slack, GitHub, Jira, or Notion principal
IF Devin places secrets or source code into files or messages that Kestra can read or log
mitigations: Separate OAuth principals for each agent
Block Kestra from reading Devin workspace files
Redact secrets before any handoff
Limit Kestra logging for agent-originated inputs
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention rules

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have unrestricted filesystem write and shell execution, and Devin also modifies git state while Kestra can run workflows with root and docker.sock. In a shared repo or workspace, concurrent writes can corrupt state or overwrite each other, and the elevated privileges make recovery harder. This is a default-dangerous overlap, so high fits.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository or storage path
IF either agent performs concurrent git or filesystem mutations without locking
mitigations: Assign disjoint directories or repos
Serialize write access with a lock or queue
Disable root/docker.sock for routine runs
Use branch-per-agent workflows
requires-engineering: add optimistic concurrency control for shared mutable resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: Devin can generate code, docs, and task outputs; Kestra can trigger downstream actions across email, Slack, cloud, and databases. If Kestra treats Devin's output as authoritative, a mistaken or malicious artifact can cascade into automated external actions. Because the downstream blast radius includes notifications and infrastructure, high is justified.
conditions: IF Kestra consumes Devin-produced text, YAML, or code as workflow input
IF Kestra executes notifications, cloud actions, or database writes based on that input without verification
mitigations: Require human approval before execution
Validate Devin outputs against schemas
Add a second independent checker before actions
Restrict Kestra to dry-run mode for agent-generated artifacts
requires-engineering: implement signed, provenance-checked handoffs

E_compliance.rationale: Devin handles team chat, issue trackers, docs, and secrets in a vendor-managed cloud workspace, while Kestra can process logs, messages, notifications, and cloud storage data. If regulated or sensitive data is routed through both, retention and residency obligations can diverge. The profiles do not specify matching compliance controls, so medium is the safest choice.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into Devin integrations and then routed through Kestra logs or notifications
IF the deployment requires residency, retention, or deletion guarantees that are not configured identically
mitigations: Avoid sending regulated data through either agent
Align retention settings across integrations
Document data-flow boundaries for both agents
Purge logs containing sensitive payloads
requires-engineering: add residency and retention policy enforcement
